correctness.rationale: Over odd fields, scalar square-sum and noncommutation force both traces to be zero. Invertible traceless matrices of prescribed square \(dI_2\) number \(q^2+q\chi(d)\) for nonzero \(d\). Two explicit quadratic-character convolutions give \(T(0),T(c)\); all commuting traceless invertible pairs are \(V=tU\) with nonzero \(t\), and their count \(C(c)\) follows from \(\sum_{t\ne0}\chi(1+t^2)=-2\). Subtracting gives the formulas for zero and nonzero targets. All boundaries and positivity for \(q\ge3\) are covered. Independent arithmetic checker exhausts full invertible pairs at orders 3 and 5 and traceless pairs at orders 7, 9, and 11; the symbolic steps prove the infinite case.

value.rationale: The current matrix-Waring study motivates the difficult square-exponent case, which falls outside its coprime-exponent theorem. This exact theorem answers the natural complete central-target census over every odd finite field while retaining both invertibility and noncommutation. Trace rigidity gives a structural mechanism, and the character-separated three-level counts quantify representation redundancy, including the smallest field and both square classes. It is an infinite-family exact invariant, not a routine numerical sample.
